content.value_statement: Paid media teams lose efficiency when campaigns, keywords, and organic traffic overlap. This skill designs a clear account structure with campaign types, match types, negatives, and handoff notes.
actual_capabilities: Chooses Search, Performance Max, or broad campaign types based on the goal and readiness.
Maps ad groups or asset groups around one intent theme per group.
Plans targeting, match types, audience signals, negative keywords, and exclusions.
Audits paid and organic overlap using campaign exports and GA4 traffic acquisition data.
Scores the ROAS Audience dimension and prepares a handoff for the account auditor.
limitations: It does not compute the final RQS or enforce ROAS veto items.
It does not allocate budget or replace the budget optimizer skill.
It needs user-owned exports, pasted goals, or manually gathered evidence.
Competitor signals depend on visible ad library data and manual interpretation.

use_cases.title: Rebuild a Search Account
use_cases.description: Create a campaign and ad group map before a paid search relaunch.

use_cases.title: Choose a Campaign Type
use_cases.description: Compare Search, Performance Max, and broad match for a new acquisition goal.

use_cases.title: Audit Paid and Organic Overlap
use_cases.description: Find query themes where paid traffic may compete with existing organic traffic.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a goal and a few campaign themes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the paid account structure for my goal: [goal]. Platforms: [platforms]. Themes: [themes].

prompt_templates.title: Select Campaign Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare launch options before building campaigns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Should I use Search, Performance Max, or broad match for [goal]? Explain the tradeoffs and propose the structure.

prompt_templates.title: Build Negative Hygiene
prompt_templates.scenario: Use search term evidence to reduce waste and overlap.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these search terms and campaign themes. Build negative keywords, exclusions, and cross-campaign guardrails.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Overlap and Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Use full export context and prepare the downstream audit handoff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit paid and organic overlap using my campaign export and GA4 traffic acquisition export. Score ROAS Audience and write the handoff summary.

output_examples.input: Plan a Google Ads structure for a direct response software trial campaign.
output_examples.output: A campaign map with Search for high-intent queries, Performance Max only when feed and creative inputs are ready, themed ad groups, match type guidance, negatives, and handoff notes.

output_examples.input: Audit paid and organic cannibalization for branded and comparison queries.
output_examples.output: A query-theme overlap read that separates incremental paid coverage from likely cannibalization, with recommended exclusions and items needing more analytics data.

output_examples.input: Create a structure for prospecting and retargeting across Google Ads and Meta.
output_examples.output: A platform-specific campaign layout with audience signals, asset group themes, exclusion logic, and a ROAS Audience score for the proposed structure.

best_practices: Provide the campaign goal, platform, themes, and any current account export.
Separate intent themes before asking for match types or negative keywords.
Confirm missing exports instead of treating absent data as a pass.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to compute final RQS or enforce all ROAS veto rules.
Do not use it as the source of truth for budget allocation.
Do not rely on competitor ad libraries as precise spend or volume data.

faq.question: What platforms does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports paid advertising planning across platforms, with specific guidance for Google Ads structures and manual ad library research.

faq.question: Can it choose between Search and Performance Max?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares campaign types against the goal, intent maturity, creative readiness, and feed readiness.

faq.question: Does it calculate budgets?
faq.answer: No. It can reference budget optimizer output, but budget allocation is outside its scope.

faq.question: Does it need API access?
faq.answer: No. It can work from pasted goals and user-owned exports. Optional read-only connectors may help when available.

faq.question: What does the paid and organic audit do?
faq.answer: It compares paid query themes with organic traffic evidence to flag possible overlap and incremental coverage gaps.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the account goal, platform, themes, campaign export, search terms report, and GA4 traffic acquisition export.
